title: The Red Skelton Show
paragraphs: Comedy-variety star vehicle built around Red Skelton recurring characters, sketches and music. Frozen GRH snapshot has 266 playable objects through June 25, 1952, including 38 rehearsal recordings and two undated AFRS items; the historical radio run continued into 1953.

GRH documents the program through Raleigh Cigarette Program / NBC (October 7, 1941 to June 6, 1944) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Military-service hiatus (June 7, 1944 to December 3, 1945), Post-service NBC return (December 4, 1945 to 1949-04) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and CBS-era Red Skelton Show (1949-04 to 1953-05) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Red Skelton (performer on 90 recordings and host on 2 recordings), David Rose and His Orchestra (performer on 91 recordings), Rod O'Connor (performer on 75 recordings and announcer on 18 recordings), [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer on 88 recordings), Pat McGeehan (performer on 87 recordings), Dick Ryan (performer on 63 recordings), and The Four Knights (performer on 47 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include family and domestic comedy, music and performance, travel and transportation, radio and broadcasting, shopping and consumer life, and jobs and workplace comedy.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including World War II and entertainer military service, Sponsor-driven network comedy, and Radio-to-television transition.

Comedy-variety star vehicle built around Red Skelton recurring characters, sketches and music. Frozen GRH snapshot has 266 playable objects through June 25, 1952, including 38 rehearsal recordings and two undated AFRS items; the historical radio run continued into 1953.

GRH documents the program through Raleigh Cigarette Program / NBC (October 7, 1941 to June 6, 1944) on NBC Radio Network, Military-service hiatus (June 7, 1944 to December 3, 1945), Post-service NBC return (December 4, 1945 to 1949-04) on NBC Radio Network, and CBS-era Red Skelton Show (1949-04 to 1953-05) on CBS Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Red Skelton (performer on 90 recordings and host on 2 recordings), David Rose and His Orchestra (performer on 91 recordings), Rod O'Connor (performer on 75 recordings and announcer on 18 recordings), Lurene Tuttle (performer on 88 recordings), Pat McGeehan (performer on 87 recordings), Dick Ryan (performer on 63 recordings), and The Four Knights (performer on 47 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to CBS Radio Network (broadcast on network) and NBC Radio Network (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include family and domestic comedy, music and performance, travel and transportation, radio and broadcasting, shopping and consumer life, and jobs and workplace comedy.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including World War II and entertainer military service, Sponsor-driven network comedy, and Radio-to-television transition.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include Lux Radio Theatre (6 shared credited people), The Whistler (6 shared credited people), Let George Do It (5 shared credited people), Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar (6 shared credited people), and Dr. Christian (4 shared credited people).
